bull.b: Higher six-month revenue and a substantially smaller net loss indicate improving commercial execution versus the prior year. If Bellwright sales and deferred-revenue releases develop into repeatable demand, the company could strengthen operating leverage and move closer to sustainable profitability over the next several quarters.

Meaningful engagement across PC, console, and mobile gives Snail an established audience for updates, downloadable content, and future releases. A broad installed base can support recurring monetization and reduce reliance on acquiring entirely new users for every product cycle.

bull.t: Visible content pipeline and deferred revenue
bull.b: The deferred-revenue balance and scheduled DLC releases provide measurable revenue visibility beyond the latest quarter. Continued delivery of Genesis, Tides of Fortune, Dragontopia, and other planned content could convert existing commitments into cash receipts while sustaining engagement across the portfolio.

bear.b: Negative equity indicates an impaired capital base and materially limits financial flexibility. It can make external financing more difficult, increase refinancing and solvency pressure, and constrain the company’s ability to fund development or absorb weaker sales without further balance-sheet support.

Although margins improved from the 2025 trough, Snail remains loss-making and revenue has been volatile and recently declining. Persistent losses reduce internally generated funding for content investment, while uneven demand makes it harder to establish dependable earnings power over the medium term.

The conditional listing decision places a concrete balance-sheet requirement on the company and creates an ongoing compliance obligation. Failure to reach or maintain the required equity level could lead to delisting, increasing financing friction and distracting management from product execution and growth initiatives.
